index.title: Skill packs by context cost
index.sub: Estimated Claude Code listing tokens for 8 public skill packs, based on snapshots from 2026-11-27.

anthropics/skills.what: Anthropic's reference pack of 20 skills covering Office documents, Claude API development, visual design, and skill authoring.
anthropics/skills.pick: Pick it if a project needs Office file skills like `docx`, `xlsx`, `pptx`, and `pdf`, or Anthropic's references for `claude-api` and `mcp-builder`.
anthropics/skills.skip: Look elsewhere if only `frontend-design` is needed and 2,449 tokens of unrelated descriptions would go into the full skill listing.
post: Weighing the entire anthropics/skills repository has the largest estimated listing in this table: 2,449 tokens across 20 listed skills, with 0 manual-only entries and 288,376 body characters on disk. The cost reflects both breadth and verbose routing text, since many descriptions spell out long trigger and skip rules.

Across the repo, 13 skills trip `expensive-description` for crossing 300 characters. `claude-api` takes the top spot at 1,083 characters and 271 tokens, backed by a 103,964-character body. `academy-guide` adds 253 tokens, `discernment-nudge` adds 251 tokens, and the Office skills `xlsx`, `docx`, `pptx`, and `pdf` add 239, 211, 185, and 111 tokens. Even `template-skill` inside `template` adds 22 tokens.

Anthropic ships the repository as an open-source reference, including the document skills that back Claude's file creation alongside `skill-creator` at 84 tokens, `frontend-design` at 56 tokens, and `webapp-testing` at 56 tokens. In Claude Code, the marketplace splits into `document-skills@anthropic-agent-skills` and `example-skills@anthropic-agent-skills`, so teams can install a subset instead of loading everything.

obra/superpowers.what: An automatic development methodology that moves coding agents through brainstorming, git worktrees, written plans, TDD, and code review.
obra/superpowers.pick: Pick it if a team wants planning, test-first implementation, and verification to fire automatically across Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or other supported agents.
obra/superpowers.skip: Look elsewhere if small tasks should go straight to edits without mandatory `brainstorming` gates, or if workflows should run only on slash commands.
post: The full Superpowers listing is about 679 tokens for 15 skills, with no manual-only entries. The Claude Code plugin also injects the `using-superpowers` skill body at session start; the listing estimate does not include it. The 15 skill bodies total 139,500 characters. Only `diagnosing-superpowers` trips `expensive-description`, at 402 characters and 101 tokens, while core entries like `writing-plans` at 26 tokens and `test-driven-development` at 27 tokens stay terse.

Jesse Vincent and Prime Radiant built the pack as a mandatory process, not a menu of commands. `using-superpowers` tells the agent to check for matching skills before replying. From there, `brainstorming` settles design intent, `using-git-worktrees` isolates a branch, `writing-plans` writes out tasks, and `subagent-driven-development` or `executing-plans` implements them under red-green-refactor `test-driven-development` and `verification-before-completion`.

The README documents installs for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Pi, and other coding agents, so teams can share one workflow across tools. When a session drifts or repeats work, `diagnosing-superpowers` reads the transcript and reports what happened with line-level evidence.

mattpocock/skills.what: A composable engineering pack of 39 skills centered on grilling interviews, domain glossaries, issue-tracker specs, TDD, and deep-module architecture.
mattpocock/skills.pick: Pick it if developers want explicit slash commands for planning and ticket flows while keeping `tdd`, `diagnosing-bugs`, `code-review`, and `domain-modeling` available automatically.
mattpocock/skills.skip: Look elsewhere if every stage should trigger automatically, or if misc extras like `scaffold-exercises` and `migrate-to-shoehorn` do not belong in a full install.
post: Matt Pocock's repository has 39 skills, 168,306 body characters, and an estimated listing of 818 tokens. Its 24 orchestration skills, including `grill-me`, `grill-with-docs`, `to-spec`, `to-tickets`, `implement-spec`, and `improve-codebase-architecture`, are manual-only at 0 tokens. The remaining 15 reusable skills stay listed so the agent can pull them in on its own.

Just 2 descriptions pass 300 characters: `code-review` at 433 characters and 108 tokens, and `wizard` at 324 characters and 81 tokens. At the small end, `pr` costs 9 tokens. Installing everything also brings in repo utilities like `git-guardrails-claude-code` at 69 tokens, `setup-pre-commit` at 65 tokens, `scaffold-exercises` at 57 tokens, and `migrate-to-shoehorn` at 48 tokens, though `npx skills@latest add mattpocock/skills` allows picking specific skills.

The workflow targets recurring failure modes named in the README: misalignment, verbose domain jargon, missing feedback loops, and creeping complexity. Run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` once per repo to bind an issue tracker and doc path, then combine `grilling`, `domain-modeling`, `tdd`, `diagnosing-bugs`, and `codebase-design`.

cursor/plugins/pstack.what: Lauren Tan's Cursor and Claude Code engineering plugin of 59 skills routed through `/poteto-mode`, playbooks, and multi-model workflows.
cursor/plugins/pstack.pick: Pick it if a Cursor or multi-model setup needs near-zero idle context overhead, adversarial `interrogate` reviews, parallel `arena` and `swarm` runs, and playbooks on demand.
cursor/plugins/pstack.skip: Look elsewhere if skills should fire automatically without slash commands, or if upfront spec-and-plan gates are wanted by default.
post: By skill count, pstack is the biggest pack measured here. By estimated listing size, it is the smallest. Across 59 skills and 159,979 body characters, it has a 73-token listing and triggers 0 `expensive-description` findings. Only `setup-pstack` stays listed at 292 characters, while 58 skills are manual-only at 0 tokens.

Nothing fires until a developer invokes `/poteto-mode` or calls a skill directly, such as `/interrogate`, `/architect`, `/blast-radius`, `/arena`, `/swarm`, or `/create-formal-verification-skill`. `/poteto-mode` matches the request to a playbook, reads its inline index of `principle-*` skills, and dispatches configured models. `/setup-pstack` assigns models per role, and `/automate-me` drafts a personal mode skill from recent transcripts.

Lauren Tan built pstack for Cursor, and the repository also ships a generated Claude Code plugin under `/pstack:` prefixes. Referenced helpers like `control-cli`, `control-ui`, and `/deslop` live in `cursor-team-kit`, and the dormant `benny` automation requires Cursor. Planning is left out as a default because the author treats code as the primary spec.

vercel-labs/agent-skills.what: Vercel's official pack of 9 skills for React, Next.js, React Native, UI and docs audits, and Vercel deployment and cost optimization.
vercel-labs/agent-skills.pick: Pick it if a frontend runs on React, Next.js, or React Native on Vercel and benefits from framework performance rules alongside `web-design-guidelines`.
vercel-labs/agent-skills.skip: Look elsewhere if the stack sits outside React and Vercel, or if visual design direction and mockups matter more than engineering compliance rules.
post: Most of the 812 estimated listing tokens in vercel-labs/agent-skills go to React engineering and Vercel platform work, not general visual design. All 9 skills stay listed with 0 manual-only entries, backed by 65,764 body characters. Skills activate automatically after `npx skills add vercel-labs/agent-skills`, and changes on `main` also publish a GitHub release with a discovery index.

Descriptions on 5 skills exceed 300 characters. `vercel-react-view-transitions` costs 176 tokens across 704 characters and `vercel-optimize` costs 147 tokens across 586 characters, followed by `vercel-react-best-practices` at 90 tokens, `vercel-composition-patterns` at 86 tokens, and `vercel-react-native-skills` at 82 tokens. Smaller listings cover `vercel-cli-with-tokens` at 66 tokens, `writing-guidelines` at 58 tokens, `deploy-to-vercel` at 54 tokens, and `web-design-guidelines` at 53 tokens.

For Vercel deployments, `vercel-optimize` gathers project metrics before inspecting routes on Next.js, SvelteKit, Nuxt, or Astro, and `deploy-to-vercel` handles git-push or temporary CLI deploys. Outside React, `web-design-guidelines` still works as a standalone audit for accessibility, focus states, forms, typography, and motion.

antfu/skills.what: Anthony Fu's collection of 15 skills combining Vue, Nuxt, Vite, and pnpm doc references with his own JS and TS maintenance workflows.
antfu/skills.pick: Pick it if a codebase uses Vue, Nuxt, Vite, and Vitest, or if a team wants a template that generates skills directly from upstream source docs.
antfu/skills.skip: Look elsewhere if the project sits outside the Vue and Vite stack, or if general workflows tested across other ecosystems are needed instead of a doc-generation proof-of-concept.
post: Anthony Fu's pack splits between hand-maintained maintainer tools and framework references generated from cloned upstream documentation. All 15 skills are listed, with no manual-only entries: about 913 listing tokens and 75,535 body characters. Just 2 descriptions pass 300 characters: `antfu-issue-triage` at 351 characters and 88 tokens, and `antfu-simplify` at 346 characters and 87 tokens.

The hand-maintained skills cover `antfu` at 63 tokens for JS and TS conventions, `antfu-create-pr` at 63 tokens, `antfu-upgrade-deps` at 68 tokens for `taze` upgrades, `antfu-query` at 73 tokens, `antfu-simplify`, and `antfu-issue-triage`. The doc-generated skills cover `nitro` at 72 tokens, `pnpm` at 67 tokens, `vue` at 55 tokens, `vite` at 49 tokens, `pinia`, `unocss`, and `vitest` at 47 tokens each, `nuxt` at 44 tokens, and `vitepress` at 43 tokens.

The README describes the repo as a proof-of-concept for keeping skills synced with source docs, and Anthony Fu notes he has not fully tested every skill in practice. Install directly via `pnpx skills add antfu/skills --skill='*'`, sync through `@antfu/skills` and `skills-npm`, or fork the repo to generate custom doc skills.

ibelick/ui-skills.what: A pack of 11 design-engineering skills for UI cleanup, accessibility, motion performance, metadata, interactive canvases, and product visuals.
ibelick/ui-skills.pick: Pick it if a team wants framework-agnostic UI polish, `DESIGN.md` extraction, motion and accessibility fixes, or launch visuals and component canvases.
ibelick/ui-skills.skip: Look elsewhere if a repo needs React or Next.js performance internals, deployment tooling, or a general coding workflow.
post: Every token in ibelick/ui-skills pays for interface craft and presentation. The full listing for all 11 skills is about 708 tokens with 0 manual-only entries and 97,941 body characters, though teams that want a smaller footprint can keep only `ui-skills-root` at 30 tokens and fetch individual skills on demand through `npx ui-skills` or the registry MCP server.

In the full install, 4 descriptions cross 300 characters: `photographing-software` at 415 characters and 104 tokens, `create-design-md` at 395 characters and 99 tokens, `improve-ui` at 377 characters and 94 tokens, and `fixing-metadata` at 360 characters and 90 tokens. Shorter entries cover `device-frames` at 71 tokens, `fixing-motion-performance` at 63 tokens, `fixing-accessibility` at 61 tokens, `baseline-ui` at 41 tokens, `component-canvas` at 33 tokens, and `create-canvas` at 22 tokens.

`create-design-md` and `improve-ui` keep auditing separate from code edits: `create-design-md` writes a `DESIGN.md` without touching product source, and `improve-ui` stays read-only while writing implementation plans for another agent. Direct fixes live in `baseline-ui`, `fixing-accessibility`, `fixing-motion-performance`, and `fixing-metadata`.

humanlayer/skills.what: A compact set of 7 Claude Code and Codex skills covering fresh-session research-and-implement workflows, `CLAUDE.md` tuning, visual explainers, and scheduled agent loops.
humanlayer/skills.pick: Pick it if a team wants a lightweight, cherry-pickable toolkit for phased `rpi` documents, `CLAUDE.md` rewrites, or scheduled coding-agent loops without adopting a large workflow system.
humanlayer/skills.skip: Look elsewhere if a project wants built-in TDD, systematic debugging, or automated code review across every task.
post: At 7 skills and 57,043 body characters, HumanLayer's pack is the smallest repository in this table. The full listing is about 189 tokens across 6 listed skills and 1 manual-only skill, with 0 `expensive-description` findings. Its longest listing, `design-control-loop`, is 238 characters and 60 tokens.

The README guides teams to install one skill at a time via `npx skills add humanlayer/skills --skill SKILLNAME`. `rpi` researches a change, works through design choices, and implements from local documents in fresh sessions by default. It runs as `/rpi` in Claude Code and `$rpi` in Codex. `design-control-loop` at 60 tokens and `build-iterated-agentic-loop` at 43 tokens set up local components and GitHub Actions workflows for scheduled agent runs.

Narrower skills fill out the repo: `improve-claude-md` rewrites `CLAUDE.md` with `<important if>` blocks at 28 tokens, `narrow-react-prop-types` trims React props to live code paths at 22 tokens, and `show-me` creates diagrams and HTML sketches at 0 tokens. Both `visual-pr` at 19 tokens and `rpi` at 17 tokens tell the model to wait for explicit invocation instead of setting `disable-model-invocation: true`.

workflow.title: Workflow skill packs compared
workflow.sub: How obra/superpowers, mattpocock/skills, cursor/plugins/pstack, and humanlayer/skills trade automatic triggers against estimated listing size.
post: Listing size tracks which skills can invoke automatically, not how many files sit in the repo. cursor/plugins/pstack has an estimated 73-token listing: 58 of its 59 skills are manual-only and only `setup-pstack` is listed. humanlayer/skills lists 6 of 7 skills at 189 tokens. obra/superpowers lists all 15 skills at 679 tokens, not counting its startup hook. mattpocock/skills lists 15 reusable skills at 818 tokens and keeps 24 orchestrators manual-only.

Those numbers reflect distinct bets on developer control. obra/superpowers fires automatically from the first prompt via `using-superpowers`, enforcing `brainstorming`, git worktrees, written plans, and red-green-refactor `test-driven-development` without slash commands. mattpocock/skills starts from explicit commands like `/grill-with-docs`, `/to-spec`, `/to-tickets`, or `/improve-codebase-architecture`, while leaving `tdd`, `diagnosing-bugs`, `code-review`, and `domain-modeling` listed for the model.

pstack pushes manual invocation furthest and drops upfront planning as a default. It routes work through `/poteto-mode`, playbooks, multi-model `interrogate` reviews, and `arena` or `swarm` parallel runs. humanlayer/skills avoids an all-in-one methodology and offers pick-and-choose skills for fresh-session `rpi` phases, `CLAUDE.md` edits with `improve-claude-md`, visual explainers, and scheduled agent loops.

verdict.line: Best for teams that want automatic planning, worktree isolation, red-green-refactor TDD, and review across many coding agents without typing slash commands.
Best for engineers who want slash-command control over grilling interviews, domain glossaries, issue-tracker tickets, and deep-module refactors.
Best for Cursor and multi-model setups that want a 73-token Claude Code listing estimate and rigorous playbooks triggered through `/poteto-mode`.
Best for Claude Code and Codex teams that want a minimal 7-skill toolkit for fresh-session `rpi` phases, `CLAUDE.md` tuning, and scheduled agent loops.

ui.title: UI skill packs compared
ui.sub: How ibelick/ui-skills, vercel-labs/agent-skills, and anthropics/skills compare on listing size and interface work.
post: None of these packs marks any skill manual-only, so the estimate includes every description. Each pack trips `expensive-description` over 300 characters. The full listings are estimated at 708 tokens for ibelick/ui-skills (11 skills, 4 findings), 812 for vercel-labs/agent-skills (9 skills, 5 findings), and 2,449 for anthropics/skills (20 skills, 13 findings).

The gap comes from how much non-UI material each repository bundles. Every skill in ibelick/ui-skills targets interface craft: `baseline-ui`, `improve-ui`, `fixing-accessibility`, `fixing-motion-performance`, `fixing-metadata`, `create-design-md`, canvases, and launch visuals like `device-frames` and `photographing-software`. Teams can also install only `ui-skills-root` at 30 tokens and fetch individual skills through `npx ui-skills` or MCP.

vercel-labs/agent-skills pairs `web-design-guidelines` at 53 tokens with React, Next.js, and React Native engineering rules plus Vercel tools like `vercel-optimize` at 147 tokens and `deploy-to-vercel` at 54 tokens. anthropics/skills includes `frontend-design` at 56 tokens, `webapp-testing` at 56 tokens, `web-artifacts-builder` at 79 tokens, and `theme-factory` at 70 tokens alongside `claude-api` at 271 tokens and Office document skills. In Claude Code, installing `document-skills@anthropic-agent-skills` or `example-skills@anthropic-agent-skills` separately avoids listing all 20 skills.

verdict.line: Best for framework-agnostic UI polish, accessibility and motion fixes, `DESIGN.md` extraction, or on-demand loading through `ui-skills-root`.
Best for React, Next.js, React Native, and Vercel frontends that want performance, View Transitions, and deploy skills alongside `web-design-guidelines`.
Best for teams that want `frontend-design`, Playwright `webapp-testing`, or multi-component `web-artifacts-builder` alongside Anthropic's document and Claude API skills.
